metaTitle: Allergy Symptoms, Causes, and Treatment - Victory Medical Services & Medical Spa

blocks.html: Allergic Rhinitis is a type of inflammation in the nose which occurs when the immune system overreacts to allergens in the air.
Allergic Rhinitis, commonly known as hay fever or allergies), can cause a variety of symptoms and be uncomfortable to deal with. Common allergy symptoms include:
Allergic Rhinitis is often diagnosed by your physician based on your symptoms as well as medical history.

Allergic Rhinitis can often be treated with over the counter medications, but sometimes allergic rhinitis can cause some discomfort and prescription medications can help alleviate those symptoms. Antihistamines are commonly used to treat allergic rhinitis and can be found in various forms to help alleviate many of one’s symptoms. Examples of such include eye drops, nasal sprays as well as oral tablets and syrup. Some patients need extra help combating their symptoms and may be prescribed steroids or bronchodilators to help reduce those symptoms. Victory Medical has a full range of allergy services.

blocks.text: Common Supplements Found in Our Pharmacy to Help Combat Symptoms

blocks.html: Quercetin This flavonoid helps give fruits and vegetables their color and also helps stop the production of histamines which are what trigger the symptoms you experience when you have allergic rhinitis.
Butterbur This supplement has been used to treat excess mucus production.
Probiotics modify the intestinal flora in the gut and can help improve the immune system which may help in the prevention of allergies.
Spirulina stops the release of histamine that causes the uncomfortable symptoms.
Zinc helps to boost the immune system which can also help prevent the symptoms of allergies from worsening.

Allergic Rhinitis can often be prevented by avoiding the specific allergens that are triggering the symptoms as well as washing the nasal passages with a nasal saline rinse. Victory Medical offers allergy prevention treatment such as desensitization which helps introduce the body to the allergens in a controlled environment and allows the body to build up antibodies for preventing the symptoms in the future. Ask your doctor about if  you might be a candidate for this type of treatment.
